w: A single room off Kotor's old town square crams in cat-themed postcards, coins, paintings and ephemera gathered over decades, reflecting the city's centuries-old reverence for street cats as protectors of Venetian trading ships. Kotor's alleys still host dozens of resident cats the museum quietly celebrates.
s: A one-room shrine to Kotor's beloved street cats
_facts: Tiny obsessive collection tucked into a square already full of actual cats

w: French colonial-era taxidermy, tigers, gibbons, a Sumatran rhino skull, fills glass cases on the upper floor of a Hanoi science building, largely unchanged since the collection was assembled under French rule. Visits require an appointment with the museum director, keeping crowds essentially nonexistent.
s: Century-old French colonial taxidermy, by appointment
_facts: An appointment-only relic collection hidden inside a working university building

w: More than ten thousand graves, many with engraved portraits unusual in Islamic Central Asia, mark the burial ground of Bukhara's Bukharan Jewish community, one of the world's oldest Jewish diaspora populations. Most descendants now live in Israel or New York, but caretakers still maintain the site.
s: Ten thousand graves of a nearly vanished community
q: Old Jewish Cemetery of Bukhara Bukhara
_facts: Physical record of the Bukharan Jewish diaspora, largely emptied out yet still tended

w: One of roughly 130 secondhand bookshops packed into Jimbocho, the neighbourhood Time Out crowned the world's coolest in 2025. Founded in 1913, Isseido trades in antique woodblock prints, old maps and first editions across three narrow floors, a working archive of Tokyo's century-old book town.
s: Antiquarian anchor of the world's coolest book town
_facts: Named world's #1 coolest neighbourhood by Time Out in 2025, largely for its bookshops

w: A bookshop-gallery on the Menilmontant hillside stocking 22,000 titles heavy on illustration, fanzines, silkscreen prints and graphic novels alongside literature and social science. Its back room doubles as an exhibition space for young illustrators, anchoring a district Time Out flagged as newly cool.
s: Illustration-heavy indie bookshop on Belleville's slope
_facts: Menilmontant named among Time Out's coolest neighbourhoods in the world 2025

w: A bright, lively bookshop on a quiet Labone side street stocking African literature, academic titles and children's books, run as a community hub with regular readings. It anchors Labone, singled out by Time Out in 2025 as one of Accra's coolest pockets for its mix of bookshops, bars and courtyard restaurants.
s: Community book haven in Accra's rising Labone quarter
_facts: Labone named one of Time Out's coolest neighbourhoods in the world for 2025

w: Fifty-plus independent stalls trading vintage clothing, records and street food inside a graffiti-clad Victorian custard factory, the former Bird's works that now anchors Digbeth's creative quarter. Digbeth placed 13th on Time Out's 2025 coolest-neighbourhoods list and a huge new food hall is landing here.
s: Indie market inside a graffiti-wrapped Victorian factory
q: Red Brick Market, Custard Factory Birmingham
_facts: Digbeth ranked 13th coolest neighbourhood in the world by Time Out in 2025

w: A cavernous 1866 ironworks turned nonprofit cultural centre where working artist studios, a radio station and a science lab sit beside a free public gallery of ambitious contemporary shows. It helped make Red Hook, cut off from the subway, one of Time Out's coolest neighbourhoods in the world for 2025.
s: Artist-studio powerhouse in cut-off, cool Red Hook
_facts: Red Hook named a top-15 coolest neighbourhood in the world by Time Out 2025

w: A design studio and creative agency whose team includes artists with Down syndrome, autism and other conditions working alongside illustrators and art directors on branding and public murals. Based in the Mattelsa textile building, it anchors Perpetuo Socorro, named one of Time Out's coolest neighbourhoods for 2025.
s: Inclusive design studio behind a textile-district revival
_facts: Perpetuo Socorro named a Time Out coolest neighbourhood in the world 2025

n: Objectifs Centre for Photography and Film
w: An independent gallery and screening space on Middle Road showing documentary photography and short film from emerging Southeast Asian artists, with a reading room and darkroom open to the public. It sits in Bencoolen, the arts-school district Time Out named among the world's coolest neighbourhoods in 2025.
s: Indie photo and film gallery in Singapore's arts quarter
q: Objectifs Centre for Photography and Film Singapore
_facts: Bencoolen named a Time Out coolest neighbourhood in the world for 2025

w: The retail arm of the acclaimed comics and graphic-novel publisher, stocking literary fiction, art books and an outstanding wall of independent zines and international comics on rue Bernard. It anchors Plateau-Mont-Royal, ranked among Time Out's coolest neighbourhoods in the world for 2025.
s: Publisher-run bookshop stacked with zines and comics
_facts: Plateau-Mont-Royal named a Time Out coolest neighbourhood in the world 2025

w: A working streetcar depot turned museum housing restored trams and trolleybuses from the city's old electric transit network, reachable by footbridge from Portales. The neighbourhood's mix of industrial history and pulque bars made it one of Time Out's coolest in the world for 2025.
s: Vintage tram depot museum linked to Portales by footbridge
_facts: Portales named a Time Out coolest neighbourhood in the world for 2025

w: A once-nomadic project space that found a permanent home in a Little River warehouse, giving Miami's career artists solo shows outside the fair-driven Wynwood machine. It sits in a district Time Out named one of the world's coolest neighbourhoods for 2025, thanks to its unpolished galleries and cafes.
s: Formerly nomadic gallery now rooted in scrappy Little River
_facts: Little River named a Time Out coolest neighbourhood in the world for 2025

w: An internationally ranked contemporary art gallery occupying a converted warehouse on Rua Barra Funda, showing Brazilian and international artists across cavernous industrial rooms. It anchors Barra Funda, named third-coolest neighbourhood in the world by Time Out in 2025 for its creative, post-industrial vibe.
s: Blue-chip gallery in a converted Barra Funda warehouse
_facts: Barra Funda ranked 3rd coolest neighbourhood in the world, Time Out 2025

w: A project space on Kattenberg showing painting and drawing by emerging Belgian and international artists in a rough, unpretentious room, part of the gallery cluster that turned Borgerhout into Antwerp's creative heart. Time Out ranked Borgerhout the second-coolest neighbourhood in the world for 2025.
s: Rough-edged gallery driving Antwerp's Borgerhout revival
_facts: Borgerhout ranked 2nd coolest neighbourhood in the world, Time Out 2025

w: A crammed Milwaukee Avenue shop mixing used vinyl across every genre with vintage toys, horror memorabilia and its own horror-themed coffee bar next door. It anchors Avondale, a working-class Chicago neighbourhood Time Out named one of the world's coolest for 2025 on the strength of shops exactly like this.
s: Vinyl and horror toys under one Avondale roof
_facts: Avondale named a Time Out coolest neighbourhood in the world for 2025

w: A small storefront near the Columbia Street waterfront founded in 2024, fast becoming a favourite for indie, punk and post-punk collectors thanks to a tightly curated crate and an in-house reissue label. It sits minutes from Red Hook, one of Time Out's coolest neighbourhoods in the world for 2025.
s: New-wave record shop steps from the Red Hook waterfront
_facts: Fast-rising indie/punk vinyl shop opened 2024 near Red Hook

w: A specialty grocer and cafe inside the Arcoris complex stocking imported organic produce, small-batch pantry goods and a deli counter, part of the wave of concept grocers redefining Mont Kiara's food scene. Time Out named Mont Kiara one of the world's coolest neighbourhoods for 2025 for this kind of curated retail.
s: Concept grocer anchoring KL's Mont Kiara food scene
_facts: Mont Kiara named a Time Out coolest neighbourhood in the world for 2025

w: One of the most photogenic branches of the Jakarta chain credited with popularising kopi susu, Indonesia's iced coffee-and-palm-sugar drink, serving it from an airy indoor-outdoor space on Jalan Kemang Raya. It sits in Kemang, named one of Time Out's coolest neighbourhoods in the world for 2025.
s: Flagship kopi susu house in Jakarta's cafe district
_facts: Kemang named a Time Out coolest neighbourhood in the world for 2025

w: A newly opened food hall on Date Street gathering smashburger, sundae and global street-food stalls under one roof from Southern California operator Tiger Hospitality, the latest addition to Little Italy's dense dining scene. It opened in June 2026, one of the freshest additions to San Diego's food-hall boom.
s: Newly opened multi-stall food hall in Little Italy
q: Global Fork Food Hall San Diego
_facts: Opened June 2026, part of a wave of new US food halls

w: A food hall on the ground floor of the historic Bulletin Building opposite 30th Street Station, opened Halloween 2025 with emerging local chefs and a mission to provide thousands of free meals to food-insecure college students. Part of the Schuylkill Yards redevelopment reshaping University City.
s: Mission-driven food hall opposite 30th Street Station
_facts: Opened October 2025, a standout new US food hall with a social mission

w: A dog-friendly roastery and brunch spot inside the old Linden hotel building on 7th Street, ranked 89th among the world's top 100 coffee shops in 2025. It anchors Linden, named one of Time Out's coolest neighbourhoods in the world for 2025 alongside its art bars and vintage stores.
s: Top-100 roastery inside an old Linden hotel building
_facts: Ranked in the world's top 100 coffee shops 2025; Linden a Time Out pick

w: A six-storey mural of Diego Maradona wearing Napoli blue, painted by Mario Filardo after the 1990 scudetto and restored in 2016, looming over a tiny square now officially renamed Largo Maradona. Fans leave candles, scarves and flowers daily, making it the most visited piece of street art in the Spanish Quarters.
s: Six-storey Maradona mural over a renamed piazzetta
_facts: Restored and renamed square keep drawing pilgrims through 2025-26

w: A 1,200-square-foot mural along a back laneway off Eglinton West painted with local artist Adrian Hayles, portraying the reggae and ska musicians who built Little Jamaica: Jackie Mittoo, Bob Marley, the Skatalites and more. It turned a derelict alley into a landmark for Toronto's Caribbean diaspora community.
s: Laneway mural honouring Little Jamaica's reggae pioneers
_facts: Ongoing focal point of Little Jamaica's cultural-preservation push
